newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton Argyle output running near plan.
newsitem.headline: Ashton Argyle output running near plan.

text.p: Australian diamond miner Ashton Ltd said on Tuesday production at its 40.1 percent owned Argyle diamond mine was running close to plan at 7.04 million carats in the first quarter ended March 31.
Ashton forecasts annual production from Argyle, the world's biggest diamond mine, at 36 million carats in calendar 1997, down from 42 million carats in 1996.
First-quarter production from Argyle was close to plan despite disruptions caused by an early and heavy wet season in Australia's tropical northwest, Ashton said.
Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ-CRA owns the other 59.9 percent of Argyle and is the mine's manager.
Rain in the quarter made ore from Argyle's AK1 pipe wet and sticky, causing handling problems and an extended planned maintenance shutdown of processing plant in March, Ashton said.
"The recovery of minus 1.5 millimetre diamonds is also reducing as screening efficiency continues to improve," it said.
"The high rainfall also resulted in early stoppage of alluvial mining operations and made the stockpiled material harder to treat," the company said.
